chunks: Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the deviation of our companions toward the left from the qiblah, and about the reason for it.

He said: «When the Black Stone was sent down from Paradise and placed in its position, the boundary markers of the Haram were set according to where the light reached—the light of the Stone. So it is four miles on the right side of the Kaʿbah and eight miles on its left side, all together twelve miles. Thus, when a person inclines to the right, he exits the limit of the qiblah because of the lesser extent of the boundary markers of the Haram; but when a person inclines to the left, he is not outside the limit of the qiblah.»

key_terms.التَّحْرِيفِ: deviation or turning away from the intended direction
key_terms.النُّورُ: the light by whose reach the sanctuary markers were determined
key_terms.الْحَجَرَ الْأَسْوَدَ: the Black Stone, described here as descending from Paradise
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary surrounding the Kaʿbah
key_terms.حَدِّ الْقِبْلَةِ: the legal boundary or limit of the qiblah direction

ai.seo_question: Why is deviation to the left of the qiblah treated differently from deviation to the right in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a juridical point concerning slight deviation from the qiblah, especially toward the left side. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام grounds the ruling in the described extent of the Haram's boundaries in relation to the Black Stone, showing why deviation to the right is more restrictive than deviation to the left.
